name: net
doc:
The Zell-source net (see sema/stdsrc.rs for the rules): TCP, UDP
and Unix domain sockets, addresses and name resolution, over the
runtime's socket handles (runtime/ABI.md section 16). Blocking points
are awaits on readiness waits of the runtime's sharded I/O pollers
(rtWaitReadable/rtWaitWritable), so a task waiting for the network
never blocks a worker thread; name lookups run on the runtime's
resolver pool.

Errors: every failure of a socket operation is an OpError ("dial tcp
10.0.0.1:80: connection refused") wrapping the cause, which is one of
the sentinels ErrClosed, ErrTimeout, ErrRefused, ErrReset,
ErrUnreachable, ErrAddrInUse, ErrNotFound, ErrEOF (stdlib consts)
when the cause is one of those, so errors.Is(err, net.ErrRefused) works
through the wrap and errors.As(err, &op) finds the OpError.

items.name: Conn
items.doc:
Conn is a TCP or Unix stream connection. Copies share the socket, which
is closed by Close() (a second Close is a no-op) or when the last copy
is gone. Operations on a closed Conn fail with ErrClosed; Close wakes
operations waiting on the socket, which fail with ErrClosed too.

Reading: Read(n) returns a new slice of up to n bytes, ReadInto(buf)
fills a caller buffer (no allocation) and returns the count; both
signal the end of the stream by an empty result / 0, never by an
error. ReadExact(n) fails with ErrEOF if the stream ends first,
ReadAll reads to the end, ReadLine returns one line (ErrEOF at the
end). Writing: Write/WriteString/WriteV write everything (looping over
short writes) or fail; a deadline or timeout fails with ErrTimeout.
items.summary: Conn is a TCP or Unix stream connection.
